Qualified reflexes of the loṭ-/luṭ- roll/lie family plus the gay- gone auxiliary. Turner *lōrtati explicitly includes Pk loṭṭai rolls/sleeps and luṭṭai sleeps, with the unaspirated regional loṭ- series and Oriya noṭ- variant. The western survey geminates and n-initial variants are compared with this family without claiming that the Oriya variant is their immediate ancestor. Both constituents are included; extra hū/hūi auxiliary clauses are excluded.

The complete imperative consists of roll/lie down + go. The first member is compared with Turner *lōrtati (Pk loṭṭai/luṭṭai sleep; regional loṭ- and n-initial noṭ-); the second is jā-/jo go from yāti. The n-initial western forms are qualified comparative members of this family, preserving the source spelling rather than asserting a direct Oriya borrowing.

The unaspirated loṭ-/luṭ- lie-down verb matches Turner *lōrtati, including Pk loṭṭai rolls/sleeps and luṭṭai sleeps. These are a simple past or imperative/past pair of the same verb; no independent go auxiliary is present.

The complete compound is sleep/lie down + gone. Turner supplies the sov-/so- sleep family under svapiti and the gay- past of go under gata. Both constituents are linked in order, including the local vowel variants.
The entire imperative is sleep/lie down + go: svapiti through soy-/so- plus yāti through jā-. Both ordered components are saved.
